headline: Meta enters AI cloud market: neocloud rivals CoreWeave and Nebius crater
summary: Meta Platforms' announcement of 'Meta Compute'—a plan to sell surplus GPU capacity and hosted AI model access—sent shockwaves through the neocloud sector on July 1. CoreWeave (CRWV) fell 13.92% to $85.69 and Nebius (NBIS) dropped 17.01% to $229.18 as Wall Street reassessed customer concentration risks: Nebius holds a $27B Meta deal while CoreWeave has a $21B Microsoft contract.
key_facts: Meta Compute: plan to sell surplus GPU capacity and hosted AI models
CoreWeave (CRWV) -13.92% to $85.69
Nebius Group (NBIS) -17.01% to $229.18
IREN also fell ~14%
Nebius has $27B Meta customer concentration
CoreWeave has $21B Microsoft customer concentration
Meta can enter GPU rental market without GPU-collateralized debt burden

headline: CoreWeave stock tumbles 14% as Meta cloud report shakes AI compute trade
summary: CoreWeave shares fell 14% as the Bloomberg report on Meta's cloud computing ambitions raised questions about the viability of the neocloud GPU rental business model. The AI compute trade—which saw CoreWeave and Nebius surge earlier in 2026 on hyperscaler contracts—came under acute pressure as the market priced in potential competition from Meta's vast AI infrastructure.
key_facts: CoreWeave -14% on Meta cloud report
Neocloud GPU rental business model under competitive pressure
Meta's fleet rivals or exceeds CoreWeave/Nebius current capacity
Meta entering without the GPU-collateralized debt neoclouds carry
AI compute trade narrative disrupted

headline: Dollar strengthens; DXY at 101.40 as hawkish Fed and strong jobs data support greenback
summary: The US Dollar Index held at 101.40 on July 1 as the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance continued to support the greenback relative to G10 peers. The euro remains in a fade-strength dynamic against the dollar while the Japanese yen, which has the strongest policy tailwind among major currencies, has a firmer foundation than more risk-reactive currencies.
key_facts: DXY at 101.40, testing 15-month highs
Fed hawkish stance supports dollar vs G10
EUR/USD: fade-strength vs USD, price below weekly trend band
JPY: strongest policy tailwind among major G10 currencies
USD dominant over past month (+2.19%) and past year (+4.77%)

headline: FOMC April 2026 minutes: median path shows two rate cuts over next year, later than prior forecast
summary: The April 2026 FOMC minutes revealed that the median participant projection continued to show two 25 basis-point rate reductions over the next year, but respondents expected them to occur later than in the previous survey—now expected in Q3/Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, reflecting persistent inflation concerns. The committee emphasized data dependence amid uncertainty over trade and labor market dynamics.
key_facts: Median FOMC path: 2 rate cuts over next 12 months
Cuts expected later than previous survey (Q3/Q4 2026 or Q1 2027)
Fed funds rate: 3.5-3.75%
Data dependence emphasized
Inflation remains elevated, labor market solid
Trade uncertainty a key risk factor
